supported_claims.applicability: Applies to overlapping targets and repeated requests.

feature_results.external_baseline_summary: A deterministic bulk workflow uses one operation identity, per-item state and idempotency keys, declared atomic or best-effort policy, durable compensation plans, semantic locks, resumable recovery, and a final aggregate receipt including manual-recovery residue.

Specify lock scope, stop/continue rule, compensation order, resume cursor, manual recovery receipt, and late cancellation semantics.

feature_results.external_baseline_summary: A mature storage-recovery contract combines atomic crash-tested writes, immutable backup snapshots, verified restore rehearsals, quarantined corruption with authorization, versioned reconciliation, leased locks, bounded shutdown and flush, deterministic disk-full cleanup, and governed trace retention/redaction.
confirmed_gaps: Backup transaction atomicity and failed-restore rollback are undefined.
Fallback stores lack a reconciliation protocol.
Corruption deletion lacks quarantine and authorization.
Shutdown timeout and partial-flush outcomes are undefined.
underspecifications: Lock lease and steal rules, disk-full cleanup guarantees, trace redaction/retention, destructive confirmation, and recovery ownership are absent.
missed_failure_modes: Backup captures mutually inconsistent stores.
Restore fails after partially replacing the active root.
A stale lock is stolen while its owner still writes.
Disk-full cleanup deletes the only recoverable state.
A shutdown timeout leaves some stores durable and others unflushed.
feature_results.conclusion_change_summary: External evidence confirms all listed gaps and unifies them under missing transaction, authority, and recovery-oracle contracts; the feature remains critical and materially broader than checksum validation.
proposed_spec_deltas: Define a backup transaction that freezes or versions every participating store, writes a manifest of roots and digests, commits atomically, and never replaces the last certified backup until test restore passes.
Restore into a staging root, verify checksums and domain invariants, atomically switch the active root, and preserve the prior root until a success receipt; roll back the switch on failure.
Define corruption quarantine with evidence, actor authority, appeal/restore path, and no deletion before replacement durability is proven.
Use owner/token/lease/heartbeat locks with bounded stale detection and fenced writers; define shutdown phase deadlines and partial-flush receipts.
Specify disk-full reserve space, cleanup priority, protected artifacts, trace redaction, retention, and explicit destructive confirmation.
scenario_implications: Inject crash and disk-full at every backup, restore, reconciliation, compaction, quarantine, and shutdown boundary.
Test stale and live lock contention, fallback divergence, corrupted primary plus valid backup, corrupted backup, partial flush, timeout, and cleanup with only one recovery copy.
Run recurring full restore exercises and compare declared RTO/RPO with measured results.
adversarial_implications: Authenticate manifests and fence stale writers to prevent rollback, substitution, and split-brain corruption.
Quarantine rather than delete attacker-triggered parse failures, and require separate authorization for destructive cleanup.
Redact credentials, paths, and user content from traces before retention or export.
